learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition by students of the knowledge necessary for performing strength and stiffness calculations of parts and structures, in technical design, analysis, and testing of mechanical systems.
Identifying fundamental stresses and selecting calculation methods for different practical situations.
Developing calculation skills for verifying, dimensioning, and determining the load-bearing capacity of mechanical components.
Acquiring knowledge related to mechanical testing of materials and experimental determination of stress and strain states.

syllabus_topics: Schematizations in Mechanics of Materials (bodies, forces, supports). Hypotheses. Section method. Efforts.
Specific stresses and strains.
Higher order geometrical characteristics of plane surfaces. Definitions. Variation of moments with axis translation. Variation of moments of inertia with axis rotation. Principal moments of inertia.
Monoaxial tension and compression of straight bars. Stresses and strains in tension. Strength and stiffness calculation for axial loading. Bars of equal strength. Stresses on inclined sections.
Statically indeterminate systems in tension/compression. Bar fixed at ends axially loaded. Systems of articulated bars. Bars of non-homogeneous section. Thermal stresses. Assembly stresses.
Bending of straight beams. Pure bending (Calculation hypotheses, Navier's formula, bending strength calculation, optimal bending sections).
Bending of straight beams. Bending with shear force (Juravski's formula, calculation of tangential stresses for different section shapes). Longitudinal slip.
Bending of thin-walled open profiles. Shear center.
Beams of equal strength. Displacements of straight beams subjected to bending (differential equation of the elastic line).
Shearing of thin-walled parts. Stresses and strains. Shear strength calculation.
Crushing stresses on finite surfaces. Calculation of riveted joints. Calculation of welded joints.
Torsion of circular section bars. Stresses and strains.
Torsion of rectangular section, open and closed thin-walled profile bars. Torsion strength and stiffness calculation. Statically indeterminate systems in torsion.
General plane stress state. Principal stresses and principal directions.
Stress diagrams for straight beams. Gerber beams. Curved bars. Stress diagrams for plane frames.
Geometrical characteristics of plane surfaces.
Strength and stiffness calculation for tension/compression. Statically indeterminate systems.
Strength calculation of straight beams in bending. Displacement calculation in bending. Integration of the differential equation of the deformed mean fiber.
Conventional shear calculation (riveted joints, welded joints, keyed joints, etc.).
Strength and stiffness calculation for torsion of circular section bars. Statically indeterminate systems in torsion. Recapitulation problems.
Laboratory presentation. Health and Safety regulations.
Tensile testing of general-purpose steel. Compressive testing of cast iron. Tensile testing of alloy steel. Torsion testing of steel. Shearing of wires.
Evaluation of acquired knowledge. Recovery session for laboratory work for students with absences.
teaching_methods: Logical and deductive presentation supported by pptx presentations
assessment_rules: The final grade requires a minimum of 5. The final grade is composed of the exam grade (2/3) and the ongoing activity grade (1/3). For the written exam on theory subjects, the minimum average of the two grades is 5. For the written exam on seminar problems, the minimum average of the three grades is 5, with at least two problems passed. Attendance at lectures and seminars is mandatory for 70% of the total hours.
